answer:
I ran one job on emerald:mock, IQM's free Emerald test device. The job ID is 01a1647a-dd99-706e-aef6-cc61e744367d. It holds 4 circuits with 250 shots each. Each circuit is the kicked Ising model on all 54 qubits. Every qubit starts in 0. Each of the 3 steps applies RX(theta) to every qubit and then exp(i pi/4 ZZ) on every coupler. The 4 circuits use theta = 0, 0.2 pi, 0.35 pi and 0.5 pi.

Couplers: the real emerald lists 85 CZ couplers today. The mock lists 90, which are those 85 plus 5 more. I used only the 85 real ones, each once per step. I sent the circuits to the server as native gates (prx, cz, measure), so no compiler step could add, merge or remove a gate. Each exp(i pi/4 ZZ) is one CZ plus single-qubit Z turns. I folded those Z turns into the phases of the later prx gates, so they cost no extra gates. I read the circuits back from the server. Each one has 255 CZ gates (85 couplers times 3 steps), and every one of the 85 couplers appears exactly 3 times. Each one also has 162 prx gates (54 times 3) and measures QB1 to QB54. I checked the gate translation on a 10-qubit patch with 13 couplers. It matched the original circuit to within 2e-15.

What a perfect quantum computer would show (ideal magnetization, from a noiseless simulation of the submitted circuits):
- theta = 0: 1.000. With no field, every spin stays up.
- theta = 0.2 pi: 0.452
- theta = 0.35 pi: 0.113
- theta = 0.5 pi: 0.000. The field fully scrambles the up/down order.
So a stronger sideways field melts the magnetization faster. By 3 steps it goes from fully ordered to zero. A full 54-qubit simulation would be too large to store. After 3 steps, each qubit's value depends only on qubits at most 2 couplers away, which is at most 13 qubits. That made an exact simulation possible. Two qubits gave identical values with a wider region of 10 qubits, which supports this.

What the mock returned: 0.002, -0.028, -0.022 and 0.023. These are all near zero. The mock device does not run the circuit. It returns random bitstrings, so its numbers show nothing about the physics. Even the theta = 0 circuit, which should give all zeros, came back near zero. This run checks that the job is accepted and built correctly on all 54 qubits. It does not measure the melting. A run on the real emerald would cost credits, and noise would pull the measured values toward zero, mostly at small theta. The principle is that a transverse field competes with the spin-spin coupling. The field rotates spins away from up, and the couplings spread that disorder across the sheet. The mock job billed no credits. I did not fetch the billed seconds because the task did not ask for them.
